title: Hexadecimal by hand

milestone.title: Binary: The Language of the Machine

description:
Write:

```python
def to_hex(n)            # n >= 0 as upper-case hex digits with no prefix: to_hex(255) is "FF", to_hex(0) is "0"
def from_hex(text)       # "2A", "0x2a" or "0XBEEF": the number. A 0x prefix is optional and case does not matter
def binary_to_hex(bits)  # "1011111011101111" -> "BEEF": group the bits in fours from the right
```

`DIGITS = "0123456789ABCDEF"` gives you each digit's character: `DIGITS[11]` is `"B"`, and `DIGITS.index("B")` is 11. `text.upper()` makes text upper case; `text[2:]` is the text without its first two characters.

Do not use Python's `hex()` or `int(text, 16)`.

`text.startswith("0X")` is `True` when the text begins with `0X`. `if ...:` with an optional `else:` chooses what runs, `while len(bits) % 4 != 0:` repeats while its condition holds, and `for i in range(0, len(bits), 4):` gives `i` = 0, 4, 8, ...; `bits[i:i + 4]` is the four characters starting at `i`.
hints: `binary_to_hex`: pad the bits on the left with 0s until the length divides by 4, then turn each group of four into one digit.
rules: Work the digits out yourself instead of using `hex()`.
Work the value out yourself instead of using `int(text, 16)`.
Work the digits out yourself instead of formatting with `x`.
unitTests:
@test("to hex")
def _():
    check_eq(to_hex(0), "0")
    check_eq(to_hex(10), "A")
    check_eq(to_hex(42), "2A")
    check_eq(to_hex(255), "FF")
    check_eq(to_hex(256), "100")
    check_eq(to_hex(48879), "BEEF")

@test("from hex, with or without 0x")
def _():
    check_eq(from_hex("2A"), 42)
    check_eq(from_hex("0x2a"), 42)
    check_eq(from_hex("0XBEEF"), 48879)
    check_eq(from_hex("ff"), 255)
    check_eq(from_hex("0"), 0)

@test("binary to hex in groups of four")
def _():
    check_eq(binary_to_hex("1011111011101111"), "BEEF")
    check_eq(binary_to_hex("11000011"), "C3")
    check_eq(binary_to_hex("101"), "5")
    check_eq(binary_to_hex("100000000"), "100")
